ai.description: This species reaches 40–50 mm. It is brown with a distinct white upper lip, dark triangular markings on the back, and prominent horn-like skin projections above the eyes. Family: Megophryidae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Megophrys oreocrypta* is best distinguished by its distinct, elongated, triangular dermal horn above each eye, which is notably more prominent than in other Indian species.
ai.habitat: *Megophrys oreocrypta* inhabits primary evergreen and subtropical broadleaf forests in the Garo Hills, typically at elevations between 800 and 1,200 meters.
ai.behavior: The Garo White-lipped Horned Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged among leaf litter to ambush passing insects under the cover of darkness.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Megophrys oreocrypta* breeds in streams during the monsoon, laying small clutches of unpigmented eggs attached to the undersides of submerged rocks.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Megophrys oreocrypta* is endemic to the Garo Hills of Meghalaya, India, where it inhabits high-elevation evergreen forests between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The advertisement call of *Megophrys oreocrypta* consists of a series of short, low-pitched, metallic "tink" notes emitted from rocky streams in montane forests.
